subproblem.title: The initial velocity of a compact variation is a C¹ test field supported in K
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, U ⊆ E, φ : ℝ → E → E, ε ∈ ℝ and K ⊆ E. Suppose IsCompactVariation φ ε K holds: ε > 0; K is compact; (t, x) ↦ φ t x is C^∞ on (−ε, ε) × E; for |t| < ε, φ t is bijective with C^∞ Function.invFun (φ t); φ 0 = id; and φ t x = x whenever |t| < ε and x ∉ K. Suppose also K ⊆ U. Then the initial velocity X_φ(y) := deriv (t ↦ φ t y) 0 is a test field in U: X_φ is C¹, has compact support, and tsupport X_φ ⊆ U (in fact tsupport X_φ ⊆ K).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (φ : ℝ → Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (ε : ℝ) (K : Set (Ambient n ℓ)), IsCompactVariation φ ε K → K ⊆ U → IsTestField U (fun y ↦ deriv (fun t ↦ φ t y) 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) (a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, hence complete and Hausdorff). IsCompactVariation φ ε K consists of the fields (pos) 0 < ε; (compact) K is compact; (smooth) (t, x) ↦ φ t x is C^∞ on S := Ioo(−ε, ε) ×ˢ univ ⊆ ℝ × E; (diffeo) for t ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε), φ t is bijective with C^∞ Function.invFun (φ t); (init) φ 0 x = x; (fixed) φ t x = x for t ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε) and x ∉ K. IsTestField U Z means: Z is C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 Z), Z has compact support, and tsupport Z ⊆ U. Write Φ(q) := φ q.1 q.2 for q ∈ ℝ × E and X_φ(y) := deriv (t ↦ φ t y) 0. Only the fields pos, compact, smooth and fixed are used, together with the hypothesis K ⊆ U.

1. (The domain.) S is open in ℝ × E, being the product of the open interval Ioo(−ε, ε) and the whole space. By (pos), 0 ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε), so (0, y) ∈ S for every y ∈ E. By (smooth), Φ is C^∞ on S.

2. (Velocity formula.) Fix y ∈ E. Since S is an open neighbourhood of (0, y) and Φ is C^∞ on S, Φ is C^∞ at (0, y). In particular it is differentiable there, with Fréchet derivative DΦ(0, y) : ℝ × E → E. The curve g(t) := (t, y) satisfies g(0) = (0, y) and has derivative (1, 0) at 0. By the chain rule, the function t ↦ φ t y = Φ(g(t)) has derivative DΦ(0, y)(1, 0) at t = 0. Hence X_φ(y) = DΦ(0, y)(1, 0) for every y ∈ E.

3. (Regularity.) Since S is open and Φ is C^∞ on S, the derivative map q ↦ DΦ(q) is C¹ on S: on an open set, a C^N map has a C^m derivative whenever m + 1 ≤ N, and here 1 + 1 ≤ ∞. The affine map y ↦ (0, y) is C^∞ from E to ℝ × E and takes values in S (step 1). So the composite y ↦ DΦ(0, y) is C¹ on all of E. Evaluating a C¹ family of continuous linear maps at the fixed vector (1, 0) gives a C¹ map, because evaluation is a continuous bilinear operation. By step 2, X_φ = (y ↦ DΦ(0, y)(1, 0)). Hence X_φ is C¹.

4. (Vanishing off K.) Let y ∉ K. By (fixed), φ t y = y for every t ∈ Ioo(−ε, ε), and this interval is a neighbourhood of 0 by (pos). So t ↦ φ t y agrees with the constant function t ↦ y on a neighbourhood of 0. The derivative at a point depends only on the germ there, so X_φ(y) = deriv (t ↦ y) 0 = 0.

5. (Support.) By step 4, support X_φ ⊆ K. By (compact), K is compact, hence closed in the Hausdorff space E. Therefore tsupport X_φ = closure(support X_φ) ⊆ K. A function vanishing outside a compact set has compact support, since its tsupport is a closed subset of that compact set; so X_φ has compact support. Finally, tsupport X_φ ⊆ K ⊆ U by hypothesis.

6. (Conclusion.) Steps 3 and 5 give ContDiff ℝ 1 X_φ, HasCompactSupport X_φ and tsupport X_φ ⊆ U, i.e. IsTestField U (fun y ↦ deriv (fun t ↦ φ t y) 0). ∎

```lean
theorem compactVariation_velocity_isTestField : ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (φ : ℝ → Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (ε : ℝ) (K : Set (Ambient n ℓ)), IsCompactVariation φ ε K → K ⊆ U → IsTestField U (fun y ↦ deriv (fun t ↦ φ t y) 0) := by
  intro n ℓ U φ ε K hφ hKU
  have hS : IsOpen (Ioo (-ε) ε ×ˢ (univ : Set (Ambient n ℓ))) := isOpen_Ioo.prod isOpen_univ
  have hmem : ∀ y : Ambient n ℓ, ((0 : ℝ), y) ∈ Ioo (-ε) ε ×ˢ (univ : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) :=
    fun y ↦ ⟨⟨neg_lt_zero.mpr hφ.pos, hφ.pos⟩, mem_univ _⟩
  have hvel : ∀ y, deriv (fun t ↦ φ t y) 0 =
      fderiv ℝ (fun q : ℝ × Ambient n ℓ ↦ φ q.1 q.2) (0, y) (1, 0) := by
    intro y
    have hdiff : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q : ℝ × Ambient n ℓ ↦ φ q.1 q.2) (0, y) :=
      (hφ.smooth.contDiffAt (hS.mem_nhds (hmem y))).differentiableAt (by simp)
    have hg : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ ↦ (t, y)) ((1 : ℝ), (0 : Ambient n ℓ)) 0 :=
      (hasDerivAt_id (0 : ℝ)).prodMk (hasDerivAt_const (0 : ℝ) y)
    exact (hdiff.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt (0 : ℝ) hg).deriv
  have hcd : ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun y ↦ deriv (fun t ↦ φ t y) 0) := by
    have h1 : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun q ↦ fderiv ℝ (fun q : ℝ × Ambient n ℓ ↦ φ q.1 q.2) q)
        (Ioo (-ε) ε ×ˢ univ) :=
      hφ.smooth.fderiv_of_isOpen hS (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr le_top)
    have h2 : ContDiff ℝ 1
        (fun y : Ambient n ℓ ↦ fderiv ℝ (fun q : ℝ × Ambient n ℓ ↦ φ q.1 q.2) (0, y)) := by
      rw [← contDiffOn_univ]
      exact h1.comp (contDiff_const.prodMk contDiff_id).contDiffOn (fun y _ ↦ hmem y)
    simp_rw [hvel]
    exact h2.clm_apply contDiff_const
  have hzero : ∀ y, y ∉ K → deriv (fun t ↦ φ t y) 0 = 0 := by
    intro y hy
    have : (fun t ↦ φ t y) =ᶠ[𝓝 0] fun _ ↦ y := by
      filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhds (neg_lt_zero.mpr hφ.pos) hφ.pos] with t ht
      exact hφ.fixed t ht y hy
    rw [this.deriv_eq]; simp
  have hsupp : tsupport (fun y ↦ deriv (fun t ↦ φ t y) 0) ⊆ K :=
    closure_minimal (fun y hy ↦ by_contra fun h ↦ hy (hzero y h)) hφ.compact.isClosed
  exact ⟨hcd, HasCompactSupport.intro hφ.compact hzero, hsupp.trans hKU⟩
```
proof_key_steps: Φ(q) = φ q.1 q.2 is C^∞ on the open set S = Ioo(−ε, ε) × E, which contains (0, y) for every y because ε > 0
Chain rule along g(t) = (t, y): X_φ(y) = DΦ(0, y)(1, 0)
On the open set S, DΦ is C¹, so y ↦ DΦ(0, y)(1, 0) is C¹, hence X_φ is C¹
For y ∉ K, t ↦ φ t y is constant near 0 (field fixed), so X_φ(y) = 0
support X_φ ⊆ K with K compact and closed, so tsupport X_φ ⊆ K ⊆ U and X_φ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro)

audit.reason: The prose hypotheses and Lean proposition agree. Joint smoothness near (0,y) gives the velocity formula and C¹ regularity by the chain rule. The fixed-off-K condition gives vanishing outside K; compactness makes K closed and yields compact support inside U. Neither openness of U nor positive dimension is needed. The supplied proof is complete and independent.
